__

• ​It is literally interpreted as the dance of** ‘Mohini’.**
 
• It is one of the two classical dance forms that originated in **Kerala, **the other one being Kathakali.

• It has delicate movements and more feminine **facial expressions.**

questions.question: What is most important health benefits of Vitamin D?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Strengthening of bones and muscle.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin D **plays a crucial role in fortifying bones and muscles, as well as **bolstering the body's immune system.** Here's a breakdown of its benefits and sources:

 
 
• **Bone and Muscle Strength: **Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus, crucial minerals for maintaining healthy bones and teeth. It also aids in muscle function and strength.
 
• **Disease Resistance:** Adequate levels of vitamin D are linked to enhanced resistance against certain diseases. It supports the immune system, reducing susceptibility to infections and diseases such as heart problems.
 
• **Sunlight: **The primary source of vitamin D is sunlight. When the skin is exposed to sunlight, it produces vitamin D naturally.
 
• **Other Sources: **Besides sunlight, significant dietary sources of vitamin D include fatty fish like salmon and mackerel, fish oils, and egg yolks.
 
 
 
• These foods can contribute to maintaining optimal vitamin D levels in the body. Ensuring adequate vitamin D intake through sunlight exposure and dietary sources is crucial for overall health and well-being, benefiting bone health, muscle function, and immune system resilience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood Pressure Regulation: **Adequate levels of vitamin D have been linked to the regulation of blood pressure, potentially helping to lower high blood pressure levels.
 
• **Promotion of Rapid Growth: **Vitamin D plays a role in supporting rapid growth, particularly during the adolescent years. It contributes to bone development and growth, ensuring proper skeletal health.
 
• Heart Rate Regulation: Vitamin D may have an impact on heart health by influencing the regulation of the heartbeat. Adequate vitamin D levels may help maintain a healthy heart rate.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for equal opportunity for all citizens in the matter of employment under the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16 of the Constitution of India **safeguards **equality of opportunity in public employment**.
 
• It prohibits discrimination against citizens based on various factors including **religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, and residence**.
 
• Article 16 permits the state to implement reservations in public employment for citizens belonging to **backward classes**.
 
• Moreover, the government has the authority to enact reservation policies for any community if they are not adequately represented in service or posts under the State.
 
• This provision aims to address historical injustices and promote inclusivity in public employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 17 **of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18 **of the Constitution of India abolishes the conferring and recognition of titles.
 
• **Article 15** of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

• The allocation of these investments is determined by the fund's investment objective.

• This involves the use of specialized machinery, equipment, and skilled labor to efficiently transform raw materials into the desired products.
 
• Quality control measures are implemented throughout the production process to ensure that the finished products meet specified standards and regulatory requirements.
 
• Effective supply chain management is vital in manufacturing, as it involves coordinating activities such as raw material sourcing, production scheduling, and distribution logistics to ensure smooth operations and timely delivery of goods.
 
• Manufacturing plays a pivotal role in driving economic growth, creating employment opportunities, and contributing to the development of industrial infrastructure.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan kings turned to Buddhism and its tenet of non violence after the Kalinga war?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Ashoka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kalinga War**, a significant conflict in ancient India, unfolded between the** Maurya Empire**, led by **Ashoka**, and the independent feudal kingdom of Kalinga, situated along the east coast in present-day **Odisha** and parts of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• This brutal war resulted in a devastating loss of life, with over one hundred thousand casualties, staining the entire Daya River with the blood of the fallen.
 
• The Daya River originates from the **Kuakhai River** in Saradeipur,** Odisha**, and courses through Khordha and Puri districts before joining Chilika Lake. Following the harrowing events of the war, Ashoka, deeply moved by the suffering, embraced Buddhism and became a fervent advocate for its propagation.
 
• His conversion played a pivotal role in the global dissemination of Buddhism beyond the borders of India.
 
• The Kalinga War, a watershed moment in history, took place in 261 BC, marking one of the bloodiest battles recorded worldwide.
 
• It pitted Ashoka, a prominent Mauryan Emperor, against the ruler of Kalinga, and significantly impacted the trajectory of ancient Indian civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka**, renowned as Ashoka the Great, ruled as the third Mauryan Emperor of Magadha in the Indian subcontinent from approximately **268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• His empire encompassed a vast territory, spanning from present-day Afghanistan in the west to present-day Bangladesh in the east, with its capital situated at Pataliputra.
 
• Revered as a patron of Buddhism, Ashoka is celebrated for his significant contributions to the dissemination of Buddhism throughout ancient Asia.

questions.question: In which year Timur’s invasion of Delhi took place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1398**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Timur,** also known as Tamerlane, led an **invasion of northern India** in **1398**, targeting the **Delhi Sultanate** ruled by Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq of the **Tughlaq dynasty**.
 
• Crossing the Indus River on **September 30, 1398,** Timur sacked Tulamba and carried out a **brutal massacre of its inhabitants**.
 
• Born on April 9, 1336, Timur was a Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire across modern-day Afghanistan, Iran, and Central Asia.
 
• He claimed descent from **Genghis Khan** and embraced Islam during his reign as the** first ruler of the Timurid dynasty**.
 
• Timur's military campaigns left a significant impact on the history of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 1398, amidst internal feuds among **Feroz Shah's successors** threatening the empire's stability, Timur invaded India from the north, effectively dismantling the centralized rule of Delhi.
 
• His conquest included the destruction of the **Turkish Sultanate of Delhi,** marked by the execution of at least 50,000 captives before the Battle of Delhi.
 
• Additionally, around 100,000 residents of Delhi were taken as slaves after the battle. Timur's campaign resulted in the estimated slaughter of up to 100,000 natives, and his forces marched as far as the Ganges before his return due to issues in Western Asia.
 
• Following the invasion and plundering of Delhi, Timur retired to Samarqand, leaving behind a significant Uzbek genetic influence in North India.
 
• Throughout his conquests, which spanned Persia, Khorasan, Jurjan, Afghanistan, and Azerbaijan, Timur earned the epithet "Prince of Destruction" for his devastating military campaigns.

questions.question: Which of the following is the new alluvium deposited by floods in the Ganga Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khadar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khadar** refers to the** fresh alluvial sediment** deposited by periodic floods in the **Ganga Plain**.
 
• Also known as **"new alluvial soil," **Khadar is typically located in the floodplains of rivers such as the Ganges.
 
• It primarily consists of fine silts that are annually deposited by** floodwaters, **contributing to soil enrichment.
 
• Characterized by its fertility, Khadar soil benefits from the regular deposition of nutrient-rich sediments during flood events.
 
• It often exhibits a higher concentration of salts, derived from the river's water, which is replenished with each flooding cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Ganga Plain**, also referred to as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, spans approximately 700,000 square kilometers across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Encompassing regions of northern and eastern India, eastern Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the southern plains of Nepal, it stands as a fertile expanse.
 
• This vast floodplain is shaped by the convergence of major rivers, including the Indus, Brahmaputra, and Ganga, which traverse its expanse.
 
• Situated within the foreland basin of the Himalayas, the plain's landscape remains largely flat, characterized by soil deposits rather than mountainous terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regur soil,** commonly recognized as black soil or black cotton soil, originates from the weathering of igneous rocks within the Deccan plateau.
 
• **Bhangar **represents an older type of **alluvial soil, **characterized by its lesser fertility and sandy composition. Composed of aged alluvium, Bhangar soil tends to exhibit a darker hue.

questions.question: Which of the following cultural festivals of South India is associated with the folklore of King Mahabali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Onam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Onam,** the vibrant cultural festival celebrated in **South India**, holds deep roots in the legend of **King Mahabali.**
 
• According to local folklore, Kerala was once under the rule of the **benevolent Asura (demon) king**, Mahabali, also affectionately known as Maveli or Onathappan.
 
• Despite his demon status, Mahabali was revered for his unparalleled generosity and compassion. His reign was hailed as a golden era marked by joy, harmony, and abundance.
 
• Each year, during the** ten-day Onam festivities,** the people of Kerala eagerly anticipate the symbolic return of their beloved king.
 
• The poignant folk song **"Maveli nadu vaneedum kalam"** poignantly recounts Mahabali's selfless sacrifice and resonates deeply with the spirit of Onam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gudi Padwa,** also referred to as the Marathi New Year or Hindu New Year, is a festive occasion primarily celebrated by Marathi and Konkani Hindus. It is observed in regions such as Maharashtra, Goa, and Daman. The term "Gudi" symbolizes a flag, while "Padwa" denotes the first day of the lunar fortnight.
 
• **Ugadi,** alternatively known as Yugadi, is a significant Hindu festival marking the commencement of the New Year. It is predominantly celebrated in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka in India. The term "Ugadi" originates from the Sanskrit words "yuga" (age) and "adi" (beginning), symbolizing the onset of a new age or era.
 
• **Pongal** holds immense importance among Tamil people in Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka, and the global Tamil diaspora. Celebrated over three or four days, each day of Pongal is marked by distinct rituals. The four consecutive days are Bhogi, Surya Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kanum Pongal. This festival venerates Surya, the solar deity in Hinduism, and aligns with the occasion of Makar Sankranti.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact was signed in ______ by Congress and the Muslim League to work in alliance for representative government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1916**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lucknow Pact,** signed in** December 1916, **marked a significant milestone in Indian politics, as it brought together the **Indian National Congress (INC) **and the** All India Muslim League **in a unified demand for Indian autonomy.
 
• Led by** Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah** respectively, the **Congress and Muslim League** passed the pact on **December 29 and 31, 1916.**
 
• This historic agreement showcased Hindu-Muslim unity, representing the first joint demand for political reform from both communities to the British colonial authorities.
 
• The Lucknow Pact instilled a sense of hope and possibility for achieving Home Rule (self-government) in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The pact facilitated cooperation between the 'extremist' faction, represented by leaders like **Lal Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal,** and the 'moderate' faction, initially led by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale and later by Mahatma Gandhi **within the Indian National Congress.
 
• Overall, the Lucknow Pact remains a pivotal moment in India's struggle for independence, emphasizing unity and cooperation among diverse political factions in the pursuit of self-governance.

questions.question: The President of India decides on the question as to the disqualification of Members of Parliament in consultation with the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Election Commission of India.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The President of India **decides on the question as to the **disqualification of Members of Parliament in consultation** with the **Election Commission of India**.
 
• **Parliament (MPs), **while **Articles 191, 192, and 193** pertain to the disqualification of Members of the State Legislative Assembly (MLAs).
 
• The constitution outlines certain conditions for disqualification, including holding any office of profit under the state or central government, being of unsound mind, an undischarged solvent, or not being a citizen of India, and being disqualified according to any law of the parliament.
 
• The Parliament has established further disqualifications according to the **Representation of People Act (1951)**.
 
• The President holds the final authority for decisions regarding disqualification of MPs, while the Governor holds this authority for MLAs.
 
• However, in both cases, the opinion of the Election Commission of India must be obtained. MPs or MLAs can also be disqualified on the grounds of defection (Schedule X, Articles 102 and 191), with decisions made by the Chairman in the case of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker in the case of the Lok Sabha for Parliament, and the Chairman in the case of the Legislative Council and the Speaker in the case of the Assembly for State Legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Election Commission of India** was established on January 25, 1950.
 
• **Articles 324 to 329,** falling under Part XV of the Indian Constitution, outline its provisions.
 
• Headquartered in New Delhi, the Election Commission of India is led by a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. Sukumar Sen served as the first Election Commissioner of India.
 
• The appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners is made by the President.

questions.question: Mohenjodaro site of Harappan civilisation is situated on the bank of which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohenjo-daro **is situated on the right (west) bank of the lower** Indus River **in **Larkana District**, **Sindh, Pakistan**.
 
• Positioned on a Pleistocene ridge within the floodplain of the Indus, it lies approximately 28 kilometres (17 mi) from the town of Larkana.
 
• This archaeological site, built **around 2500 BCE**, represents the largest settlement of the **ancient Indus Valley Civilization **and stands as one of the earliest major cities in the world.
 
• It flourished contemporaneously with civilizations in ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, Minoan Crete, and Norte Chico.
 
• Mohenjo-daro remained undiscovered until the 1920s, and since then, extensive excavation has been carried out at the site.
 
• In recognition of its historical significance, Mohenjo-daro was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980, marking it as the first such site in South Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indus River** is a** transboundary river** spanning across Asia, serving as a vital waterway in **South and Central Asia**.
 
• Stretching over 3,120 kilometers (1,940 mi), the river originates from mountain springs northeast of Mount Kailash in Western Tibet.
 
• It then traverses northwestward through the disputed region of Kashmir before sharply bending to the left beyond the Nanga Parbat massif.
 
• Continuing its course, the river flows south-by-southwest through Pakistan, ultimately reaching the Arabian Sea near the port city of Karachi.
 
• The northern section of the Indus Valley, along with its tributaries, constitutes the Punjab region of South Asia, while the lower reaches of the river culminate in a vast delta located in the southern Sindh province of Pakistan.

questions.question: Haripriya Namboodiri is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Kathakali__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Haripriya Namboodiri** stands out as a unique figure in the realm of **Kathakali,** being one of the few full-time, professional female artists in this traditional art form.
 
• She has defied long-standing norms and traditions by breaking into what has historically been a male-dominated domain.
 
• Despite her petite stature, she has garnered acclaim as a specialist in three veshams, portraying a diverse range of iconic roles such as **Kunti, Rukmini, Sita, Damayanti, Poothana, and Lalitha**.
 
• **Kathakali,** which originated in the 17th century within the kingdom of **Travancore (now Kerala), **initially found its roots in temple precincts before gaining prominence in royal courts.
 
• Rooted in the principles of Natya Shastra, the ancient treatise on dance authored by Sage Bharata, Kathakali also draws extensively from Hasthalakshana Deepika, another classical text that elucidates hand gestures.
 
• By the dawn of the 20th century, Kathakali faced the threat of extinction. It was during this critical period that renowned poet Vallaththol Narayana Menon and Manakkulam Mukunda Raja spearheaded the establishment of Kerala Kalamandalam.
 
• This institution emerged as a beacon of excellence for classical art forms, playing a pivotal role in the revival and preservation of Kathakali, ensuring its legacy endures for generations to come.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kuchipudi: **Originating from Andhra Pradesh, Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form that was conceptualized in the 17th century by Siddhendra Yogi, a gifted Vaishnava poet.
 
• **Odissi:** Indigenous to the state of Odisha in eastern India, Odissi is a classical dance form deeply rooted in the principles of the Natya-shastra.
 
• **Bharatanatyam: **Hailing from the Tanjore district of Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest and most revered classical dance forms, believed to be over 2000 years old.

questions.question: What is the name of the large supercontinent that existed 200 million years ago when all the continents were together?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Pangea__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pangea **is the name of the large supercontinent that existed **200 million years **ago when all the continents were together.
 
• **Pangaea, **the supercontinent, emerged during the **late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic periods.**

__
 
• **Linus Pauling** is recognized for successfully predicting regular **protein secondary structures **based on** hydrogen bonding,** an idea originally proposed by **William Astbury**.
 
• **Pauling and Corey** formulated a model for the conformation of **fibrous proteins called beta-keratins**, where the polypeptide adopts an extended zig-zag configuration rather than a coil, such as in the alpha-helix.
 
• All proteins in the human body can be synthesized from permutations of just **20 amino acids**.
 
• There are seven primary types of proteins: antibodies, contractile proteins, enzymes, hormonal proteins, structural proteins, storage proteins, and transport proteins.
 
• A protein molecule is composed of a lengthy chain of these amino acids, each linked to its adjacent amino acid through a covalent peptide bond.
 
• Hence, proteins are also referred to as polypeptides. Each type of protein possesses a distinctive sequence of amino acids, which remains identical from one molecule to another.
 
• Numerous proteins with diverse functions are known, each characterized by its specific amino acid sequence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emil Fischer**, a German organic chemist, is credited with the** discovery of caffeine **and other related purines.
 
• Additionally, he conducted extensive research on the molecular structures of sugars and proteins, earning him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1902.
 
• **Proteins** are comprised of amino acids, with **21 naturally occurring variants**.
 
• Secondary protein structures are stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The characteristics of protein strands vary depending on the type of hydrogen bonding present, with two common types being the alpha helix and beta sheet.
 
• The alpha helix is a right-handed coiled secondary protein structure, where the substituents of the amino acids extend outward.
 
• Hydrogen bonds form between the carbonyl oxygen and the four NH bonds below it, contributing to the stability of the helix.

questions.question: During which phase of the cell cycle does metabolic changes assemble the cytoplasmic material required for mitosis and cytokinesis?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is** __G2 Phase__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The G2 phase of the cell cycle **involves metabolic changes that assemble **cytoplasmic materials **necessary for** mitosis and cytokinesis**.
 
• This phase is followed by the **M phase**, where **nuclear division (mitosis) **is followed by **cell division (cytokinesis)**.
 
• Eukaryotic cells undergo a series of stages collectively known as the cell cycle, which includes** two gap phases (G1 and G2)**, an **S phase (synthesis)** where genetic material is duplicated, and an M phase where mitosis partitions the genetic material and the cell divides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• During **mitosis, chromosomes **replicated during the **S phase **are divided to ensure that each daughter cell receives a copy of **every chromosome**.
 
• This process results in the production of **two daughter cells **with the same genetic component as the parent cell.
 
• In actively dividing animal cells, the entire process typically takes about one hour.
 
• The final cellular division results in the formation of two new cells.
 
• Following mitosis is Meiosis II, where Meiosis I is a reduction division resulting in haploid cells with one copy of each chromosome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G1 phase:** During this phase, metabolic changes prepare the cell for division. At a specific point called the restriction point, the cell commits to division and enters the S phase.
 
• **S phase:** In this phase, DNA synthesis occurs, resulting in the replication of the genetic material. Each chromosome now consists of two sister chromatids.
 
• **G2 phase: **Metabolic changes in this phase assemble the cytoplasmic materials necessary for mitosis and cytokinesis.
 
• **M phase:** This phase involves nuclear division (mitosis) followed by cell division (cytokinesis).

The Correct answer is __**1-Methyl-3-Propylcyclohexane**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• These rules outline the systematic naming conventions, known as the** IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) nomenclature,** for organic compounds:

 
 
• **Choose the Longest Continuous Chain:** Select the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms as the parent chain.
 
• **Identify Substituents: **Any other carbon atoms or groups not included in the parent chain are considered substituents.
 
• **Number the Parent Chain: **Number the parent chain from one end to the other to locate the positions of alkyl substituents (locant numbers). Number in a way that results in the lowest possible locant numbers.
 
• **Add Substituents as Prefixes:** Add the names of alkyl substituents as prefixes to the name of the parent alkane. Separate the name of the substituent from the locant number with a hyphen.
 
• **Choose Numbering for Lowest Locant Numbers: **If numbering in both directions gives the same locants, choose the direction that results in smaller locants for substituents with alphabetical priority.
 
• **Use Numerical Prefixes for Identical Substituents:** If two or more identical substituents are present, use numerical prefixes (di- for 2, tri- for 3, tetra- for 4, and so on) before the name of the substituents.
 
• **Naming Saturated Monocyclic Hydrocarbons:** Saturated monocyclic hydrocarbons are named by attaching the prefix 'cyclo' to the name of the corresponding open-chain alkane.
 
 
 
• These rules ensure a systematic and unambiguous way of naming organic compounds based on their molecular structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• Monocyclic hydrocarbon is considered a parent hydrocarbon.
 
• The monocyclic hydrocarbon - **cyclohexane**
 
• The alkyl substituents are **methyl and propyl.**
 
 
 
• **Therefore the IUPAC name of the given compound is-**
 
 
• 1-Methyl-3-Propylcyclohexane.

• **Alloying Agent: **Gallium is alloyed with other metals to produce materials with specific properties. For instance, gallium-indium-tin alloys are utilized in liquid metal cooling systems for electronics, offering efficient heat transfer capabilities.
 
• **Nuclear Medicine:** Gallium-67, a radioactive isotope of gallium, plays a vital role in nuclear medicine for diagnostic imaging purposes. It is utilized to detect and diagnose certain diseases, aiding in medical diagnostics and treatment planning.

• **Indium** is also part of the boron family, with an atomic number of 49. Compared to gallium, indium has a lower boiling point, rendering it less suitable for applications requiring the measurement of high temperatures.

questions.question:
Identify whether the given statements about ionisation energy are correct or incorrect.

**Statement A:** The ionisation energy of an atom is the amount of energy that is required to remove an electron from an atom in the gas phase.

**Statement B:** The ionisation energy increases from top to bottom in groups and decreases from left to right across a period.

options.text: Both Statements A and B are correct
Both Statements A and B are incorrect

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only Statement A**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ionization energy,** also known as** ionization potential**, refers to the **amount of energy **needed **to remove an electron** from** an isolated atom or molecule**.
 
• Ionization energy is the energy required for **an isolated, gaseous atom** in its **ground electronic state to lose an electron**, forming a cation.
 
• It's commonly measured in** kJ/mol, **representing the energy needed for all the atoms in a mole to lose one electron each.
 
• In a **neutral atom,** removing the first electron demands less energy compared to subsequent removals.
 
• As electrons are lost, the atom's overall charge becomes positive, intensifying the attraction between the remaining electrons and the increasingly positive ion.
 
• Hence, each successive electron removal requires greater energy due to the rising positive charge of the ion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• As we progress across a period from** left to right,** ionization energy generally increases, while moving down a group, it typically decreases.
 
• This trend can be attributed to changes in atomic radius and effective nuclear charge.
 
• Across a period, atomic radii shrink and the effective nuclear charge rises. Consequently, electrons are held closer to the nucleus and experience stronger attraction.
 
• This makes it more challenging to remove an electron, necessitating higher ionization energy.
 
• When descending a group, atomic size expands, and the effective nuclear charge diminishes due to the increased distance of outer electrons from the nucleus.
 
• Consequently, it becomes easier to remove an electron, requiring less ionization energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Charan Singh**, the 5th Prime Minister of India and 5th Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, was deeply involved in the non-violent struggle for India's independence from British rule, following in the footsteps of Mahatma Gandhi. He faced imprisonment multiple times for his activism, including a 12-year jail term in 1930 for violating salt laws.
 
• **Giani Zail Singh,** the seventh President of India, served from July 25, 1982, to July 25, 1987. He actively participated in the Quit India Movement of 1942 and was deeply engaged in the Indian freedom movement, facing incarceration on several occasions for his opposition to British rule.
 
• **Morarji Desai,** the 4th Prime Minister of India (1977-79) and the country's first non-Congress Prime Minister, began his career as a Deputy Collector after graduating from the Wilson Civil Service in Bombay in 1918. Disillusioned with British justice during the Civil Disobedience Movement led by Gandhi in 1930, Desai resigned from government service and joined the struggle for independence.

questions.question: When was the National Interim Government of India formed, under Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 September 1946**__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The Interim Government, **established on **September 2, 1946**, marked the** final phase of British colonial rule **in India.
 
• Its principal objective was to function as a transitional administration until India achieved complete independence.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent freedom fighter and close associate of** Mahatma Gandhi,** spearheaded the Interim Government, holding the position of Vice President of the Executive Council.
 
• Key figures such as **Sardar Patel, Rajendra Prasad, and C. Rajagopalachari** were integral members of this administration.
 
• Despite its significance, the Interim Government encountered substantial challenges, including communal tensions, economic instability, and the imminent partition of India.
 
• Nevertheless, the Interim Government played a pivotal role in facilitating the transfer of power from British to Indian hands, laying the groundwork for the subsequent establishment of independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was a multifaceted Indian leader, known for his roles as an anti-colonial nationalist, statesman, secular humanist, social democrat, and author.
 
• Nehru emerged as a key leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s, advocating for India's independence from British colonial rule.
 
• Upon India's independence in 1947, Nehru assumed the position of the country's first Prime Minister, serving for an impressive 16 years.
 
• During his tenure, he championed parliamentary democracy, secularism, and advancements in science and technology, significantly influencing India's evolution as a modern nation.
 
• In the realm of international affairs, Nehru pursued a policy of non-alignment, steering India clear of alignment with the two blocs of the Cold War. Beyond his political leadership, Nehru was also a respected author.

questions.question: Europeans entered India with a mindset of trading only. This streak was initiated by which of the following European nations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Portuguese ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Portuguese **were the pioneering** European nation** to initiate trade with India, marking the onset of **European colonialism** in the subcontinent.
 
• Driven by a desire to dominate the** lucrative spice trade**, they established trading posts and fortified settlements along the Indian coastline.
 
• This interaction catalyzed cultural exchanges, triggered conflicts with indigenous rulers, and contributed to the transformation of Indian society.
 
• The Portuguese influence served as a precursor to centuries of European involvement and colonial governance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Europe**, a continent situated predominantly in the **Eastern Hemisphere **and entirely in the **Northern Hemisphere**, is bounded by the Arctic Ocean to the north, the Atlantic Ocean to the west, the Mediterranean Sea to the south, and Asia to the east.
 
• It shares the landmass of Eurasia with Asia and forms part of Afro-Eurasia with both Asia and Africa.
 
• The watershed of the Ural Mountains, the Ural River, the Caspian Sea, the Greater Caucasus, the Black Sea, and the Bosporus Strait are commonly regarded as the dividing line between Europe and Asia.
 
• European culture comprises a diverse array of national and regional cultures, which collectively contribute to the broader Western civilization.
 
• Ancient Greece and ancient Rome, particularly through their Christian legacies, are widely acknowledged as pivotal and shared cultural influences throughout Europe.
